preservationRule: Existing localized paragraphs 10, 11, 12, 13 and 15 are copied byte-for-byte from the current Xitsonga registry.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: A staple earns its place because it feeds the household beyond the day of harvest.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: A staple earns its place because it feeds the household beyond the day of harvest.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: A staple earns its place hikuva yi phamela ndyangu ni le ndzhaku ka siku ra ntshovelo.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: A staple earns its place because it feeds the household even after harvest day.
entries.conditions: Exact earns-place wording retained after independent rejection of a necessity shift; ordinary reason and post-harvest relation drafted.
entries.uncertainty: Independent semantic repair accepted; machine draft, no fluent approval.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: It carries energy or protein. It stores, or it stays in the ground until you need it. And often it carries cultural memory too.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: It carries energy or protein. It stores, or it stays in the ground until you need it. And often it carries cultural memory too.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Yi nyika energy kumbe protein. It stores, or it stays in the ground until you need it. Hakanyingi yi tlhela yi rhwala cultural memory.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: It provides energy or protein. It stores, or stays in the ground until needed. Often it also carries cultural memory.
entries.conditions: Translates the ordinary energy/protein and cultural-memory framing; retains the storage alternatives exact English because the wording is agriculturally specific.
entries.uncertainty: The storage alternatives remain exact English; cultural-memory term remains English.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: One staple leaves you vulnerable. Two or more give you options when weather or pests hit.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: One staple leaves you vulnerable. Two or more give you options when weather or pests hit.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Staple yin'we yi ku siya u nga sirhelelekanga. Swimbirhi kumbe ku fhira swi ku nyika tindlela to hlawula loko maxelo kumbe pests ti hlasela.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: One staple leaves you unprotected. Two or more give you options when weather or pests strike.
entries.conditions: Preserves one versus two-or-more, vulnerability, options and weather/pest trigger; keeps pests in English because the term may cover more than insects.
entries.uncertainty: Machine draft; staple and pests remain English; no fluent approval.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Grow at least two. Not one.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Grow at least two. Not one.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Byala swimbirhi kumbe ku fhira. Ku nga ri xin'we.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Grow two or more. Not one.
entries.conditions: Preserves the minimum of two and explicit contrast with one.
entries.uncertainty: Machine draft; quantity and imperative remain direct; no fluent approval.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Which staple does your household rely on most heavily right now? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Which staple does your household rely on most heavily right now? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Which staple does your household rely on most heavily right now? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Which staple does your household rely on most heavily right now? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.
entries.conditions: Whole exact English held because the most-heavily superlative was not securely conveyed.
entries.uncertainty: Original superlative candidate independently rejected; do not use it.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Each staple protects you against something different.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Each staple protects you against something different.
entries.candidateitsongaDraft: Staple yin'wana ni yin'wana yi ku sirhelela eka xilo xo hambana.
entries.drafterBacktranslation: Each staple protects you against something different.
entries.conditions: Translates the ordinary difference/protection statement; no crop-specific claim added.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Maize gives calories, and stores dry. Open-pollinated maize also lets you save your own seed, if you manage isolation and selection.
entries.currentRegistryDraft: Maize gives calories, and stores dry. Open-pollinated maize also lets you save your own seed, if you manage isolation and selection.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Beans and cowpeas give a storable protein harvest.

entries.exactSourceEnglish: Sweet potato develops some drought tolerance after its storage roots form. It needs water in the first weeks and while roots are forming; water stress then can reduce the harvest. Its young leaves are edible too.
